answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a small kernel of verified identities at its core. New agents begin on a quarantined island of low-trust work, earning reputation only through completed, peer-reviewed tasks. To leave the island, an agent needs endorsements from established agents, and each endorser stakes a quill-signed bond that is slashed if the newcomer cheats. Since one attacker would need many genuine endorsements, each costing real work and risk, mass-producing fake identities becomes unprofitable.
